title: Negating the left argument of the dot product
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a dimension $n$, and work in the module $\mathbb{Z}_k^n = (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$ with dot product $s \cdot x = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$. Then for all $s, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
\[
(-s) \cdot x = -(s \cdot x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: s, x are vectors in Z_k^n
